battle.name: 諸葛亮南征
battle.brief: 建興三年春，丞相諸葛亮率大軍南征，平定益州南部越嶂、牂柯、益州三郡的叛亂。蜀軍以弩為主要遠程火力，壓制壘上守軍、封鎖渡口與谷道，並輔以分路進兵與攻心之策；孟獲七縱七禽而心服，同年秋悉平，蜀漢由此得南中兵糧而備北伐。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 交戰的一方是蜀漢。建興三年春，丞相諸葛亮以丞相錄尚書事、假節之權率大軍南征，兵源為成都與漢中兩線的蜀漢主力，附以益州各郡縣的守兵與徵發的南中丁壯；蜀漢在益州南部設益州郡、牂柯郡、越嶂郡三郡的行政骨架，郡縣官吏多由漢人充任，軍中則以漢中、成都一線的甲兵與弓弩手為骨幹，騎兵比例偏低，故步戰與遠射是主要作戰方式。另一方是南中反叛聯盟：《三國志·蜀書·諸葛亮傳》記「南中諸郡，並皆叛亂」，《華陽國志》等書補記首領有越嶂郡的雍闓、牂柯郡的高定、益州郡的趙莋與孟獲等，各部族各守本郡山險，互通聲援，首尾相望，形成鬆散而頑強的聯軍。孟獲為夷、漢所服，是聯軍的實際核心；其妻祝融夫人所部的火攻與竹木拒馬，使蜀軍在攻壘時屢受牽制。聯軍熟悉山谷、瘴癘與水勢，蜀漢則握有兵器、糧秣與統帥上的絕對優勢，這一體格差異決定了戰爭的樣貌：短兵相接之前，先比的是糧秣、籌略與士氣，而非單純的強弱。
countriesEn: The belligerent on one side was Shu Han. In the spring of Jianxing 3 (225), the chancellor Zhuge Liang, holding the authority of the office of recorder of the imperial documents and the imperial tally, led a great army south. His troops came from the main body drawn on Chengdu and Hanzhong, augmented by the garrisons of the commanderies of Yizhou and by southern labour levies. Shu already had an administrative skeleton of three southern commanderies, Yizhou, Zangke and Yuexi, whose regular officials were mostly Han Chinese, while the field army leaned on the armoured infantry of the Hanzhong and Chengdu lines and on the crossbowmen, with a low proportion of cavalry, so that infantry action and missile fire were the dominant forms of battle. The other side was a loose southern rebel coalition. The Records of the Three Kingdoms, in the biography of Zhuge Liang, states that all the southern commanderies rebelled at once, and the Huayang Guozhi adds the names of their leaders: Yong Kai of Yuexi, Gao Ding of Zangke, Zhao Zhi of Yizhou and Meng Huo among others. Each people held the hill country of its own commandery, kept in touch with the others, and so formed a scattered yet tenacious league. Meng Huo was the man respected by both the indigenous peoples and the Han settlers and was the real core of that league; the fire-throwing and the bamboo-and-timber barriers of the people of his wife Zhurong repeatedly checked Shu's attacks on fortified positions. The rebels knew the gorges, the miasma and the waters intimately, while Shu held overwhelming superiority in weapons, supplies and command, and that asymmetry between the two sides shaped the whole campaign.
people: 總帥是諸葛亮。他以丞相錄尚書事、假節、領益州牧的身份行事，《三國志》記他「政事無巨細，咸決於亮」，南征之舉由他一人定奪：先遣使議和於吳，後自行發兵，兵罷乃奏。孟獲是決定勝負的另一端，裴松之注引《漢晉春秋》記他被生致之後，先問「此軍何如」，見營陳壯盛仍然不服，經七縱七禽才說出「公，天威也，南人不復反矣」。蜀漢方面，張嶷後任中都護、統南中軍務，李恢出守益州郡，馬忠鎮牂柯郡，李平與王平分任監軍與參軍，各統本部隨主力進止；雍闓、高定、趙莋等守土首領則各統部落抵抗。史書對諸葛亮抵南中後分兵進擊的部署記載零碎，具體孰先孰後，諸說並存，可確定的是亮本人自將主力深入不毛之地，而把後方與糧道交給可靠將領。亮出軍時隨行詔賜的金鈇鉞、曲蓋與羽葆鼓吹，標示的是丞相出征的威儀，諸將奉詔聽命，南征的調度因此能在短期內完成。
peopleEn: The supreme commander was Zhuge Liang. He acted as chancellor with the authority of the recorder of the imperial documents, the imperial tally and the governorship of Yizhou; the Records of the Three Kingdoms says that no matter of state, great or small, was settled without him, and the decision to march south was his alone. Envoys went to Wu to negotiate friendship first, and the army was raised on his own authority and reported to court only after the fighting was done. Meng Huo was the other decisive figure. Pei Songzhi's note quoting the Han Jin Chunqiu records that when he was taken alive he was first asked what he thought of the army, and though he saw the imposing camp and the formations he still would not submit; it took seven releases and seven captures before he said: 'My lord, this is Heaven's might; the people of the south will not rebel again.' On the Shu side, Zhang Yi afterwards held the office of Protectant General of the Centre and took charge of the southern commanderies, Li Hui was set over Yizhou commandery, Ma Zhong was stationed at Zangke, and Li Ping and Wang Ping served as supervisor of the army and as staff officer, each leading his own contingent in step with the main force; the local leaders Yong Kai, Gao Ding and Zhao Zhi each headed the resistance of their own districts. The records of how Zhuge Liang divided his army once he reached the south are fragmentary, and which column moved first is a matter of competing accounts; what is certain is that Liang himself led the main body deep into the wilderness while leaving the rear and the supply route in the hands of dependable officers. The gold-ribbed axes, the curved canopy and the phoenix-banner escort that accompanied him marked out the authority of the chancellor on campaign, the generals obeyed the imperial commission, and the movement was organised within a very short time.
kits: 本卡兵器是秦弩，即弩機把拉力存起來再釋放的機射武器，見於秦始皇陵陪葬坑出土的秦弩實物與同出的箭鏃，秦代已是成建制的裝備。到建興三年的蜀漢，弩是步軍唯一可靠的遠程重火力。蜀軍缺馬，遇林密山深之地，弓在狹窄處難以張滿，弩卻能預先張弦蓄力，臨陣一發而速。弩手多列於長槍、藤牌與大盾之後，掩蔽前進；攻壘時以弩壓住壘頂與城頭守軍，掩護步卒抵牆、破柵、登壘；守御則以弩封鎖渡口與谷道，令敵不得通過。攻守之外，蜀軍尚有環首刀、劍、長矛、皮甲與革甲，遇木柵草屋則備火箭焚燒；渡瀘水靠竹筏木排，糧秣靠人力背運，所以士卒多病而糧常常不繼。弩的代價是矢耗極大，每一具弩都要隨軍攜帶大量弩矢，戰後還要派人回收敵方遺矢以充軍實。秦弩的機件在秦代已有出土，說明關鍵部件早經標準化，漢承秦制，蜀漢沿用，弩兵與長槍手混編，攻守皆倚為骨幹。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Chinese crossbow, a machine bow that stores the draw force and releases it later. It is attested by crossbows actually excavated from the burial pits of the First Emperor of Qin together with the arrowheads found alongside them, so it was already an organised piece of equipment in Qin times. By the Jianxing 3 year of Shu Han the crossbow was the only reliable heavy missile weapon of the foot soldier. Shu had few horses, and in thick forest and deep mountain country a bow could hardly be drawn full in the narrow space, whereas a crossbow could be strung and cocked in advance and loosed at once on the attack. Crossbowmen were posted behind the long spear, the rattan shield and the large pavise, covering the advance; when a stockade was assaulted, crossbow fire pinned the defenders on the wall and the ramparts while the footmen closed to the stockade, broke the barrier and climbed it; on the defensive side the same weapons sealed fords and valley roads so that no enemy could pass. Beside the bow, Shu's order of battle included ring-pommelled sabres, swords, long spears, leather and hide armour, and fire-arrows for burning timber fences and thatched huts. Crossing the Luo River was done on bamboo and timber rafts and grain was carried on human backs, so the soldiers were often sick and the rations frequently failed. The crossbow's cost was a heavy expenditure of bolts: every piece had to travel with a large supply of them, and parties were sent out after each action to recover the bolts left by the enemy for reuse. Parts of the Qin crossbow mechanism have been excavated, which shows that its key components had already been standardised; the Han inherited the Qin design and Shu Han went on using it, the crossbowmen being intermingled with the pikemen and forming the backbone of both attack and defence.
tactics: 南征的戰術主線是分路進兵與攻心並用。亮不把全軍壓在一條山道上，而是令各路分道、互為犄角，一路攻略郡縣，一路封鎖谷口，一路趨向滇池，以斷其糧道與退路。裴注引《漢晉春秋》記亮到南中後「所在戰捷」，隨即生致孟獲，讓他觀看營陳，再縱之再戰，七縱七禽而終不誅，收其心而後收其地。亮答諫者所陳的三個「不易」定下全盤方略：留兵則無所食，夷新傷破而無兵留外人必生禍患，夷嫌釁重終不相信，故「不留兵、不運糧」，而「即其渠率而用之」，以當地首領充當地官吏。渡瀘在五月，正值雨季，河水暴漲，士卒「並日而食」，深入不毛之後全靠嚮導與就地向支，故史家以「五月渡瀘，深入不毛」記其艱苦。合擊的原則是每一路只求破一壘、斷一段谷道，勝則合兵，敗則退保既定渡口，不與敵糾纏於山谷深處。
tacticsEn: The tactical line of the southern campaign was advance by separated columns combined with the winning of hearts. Liang did not press his whole army along one mountain track; he sent the columns by different roads so that they supported one another, one to reduce the commanderies, one to seal the valley mouths and one to push towards Dianchi, cutting the rebels' supply lines and their retreat. Pei Songzhi's note quoting the Han Jin Chunqiu says that wherever Liang went in the south he was victorious, and that he then had Meng Huo taken alive and brought to look at the camp, released him again to fight, and after seven releases and seven captures still would not put him to death: the hearts were taken first and the territory afterwards. Liang's answer to those who advised him set out the whole plan in three 'difficulties': to keep troops would be to keep them hungry, since a garrison has to be fed; the southern people had just been broken by the war, and with no troops left behind the outsiders would surely breed disaster; and the southern people, burdened with a long record of killing and disorder, would never truly trust the outsiders. Hence 'leave no troops and carry no grain', and instead 'take their own chiefs and use them', staffing the districts with the local leaders. The crossing of the Luo came in the fifth month, in the rainy season, when the river was in spate, and the soldiers 'ate for two days on one day's rations'; once deep in the wilderness the army depended on guides and on what the country could give, so the historians recorded it in the words: 'in the fifth month we crossed the Luo, penetrating deep into the uncultivated land'. The principle of the combined stroke was that each column should only break one stockade or cut one stretch of valley road, joining forces on success and falling back on a secured ford on failure, never tangling with the enemy deep in the ravines.
data: 可核對的數字有限，但有幾條是硬證據。建興三年春出師，其秋悉平，戰事歷時約半年；孟獲七縱七禽。朝廷詔賜諸葛亮金鈇鉞一具、曲蓋一、前後羽葆鼓吹各一部、虎賁六十人，儀仗之外未見大軍人數的記載，兵眾總數史無明文。行程方面，亮自成都南下，經漢中與益州腹地而入越嶂、滇池，路以千里計。地理上，裴注引《漢書地理志》說瀘惟水出牂柯郡句町縣，五月渡瀘即在此水一帶，滇池是南征的終點。糧秣方面，亮自述「並日而食」，足見深入階段給養極緊；平定之後則是「軍資所出，國以富饒」，南中的丹砂、鹽、銅與馬匹開始穩定供應蜀漢。弩的數目沒有留下記載，只知其射速高於常弓、單兵可以連發，是蜀軍在無馬之地的核心火力。諸葛亮自己的文集《諸葛氏集》共二十四篇、一百零四萬四千一百一十二字，其第三篇題為「南征」。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, but several of them are solid. The army marched out in the spring of Jianxing 3 and everything was pacified by the autumn, so the fighting lasted about half a year; Meng Huo was released and captured seven times. The court granted Zhuge Liang one set of gold-ribbed axes, one curved canopy, one phoenix-banner and drum-and-trumpet escort before and behind, and sixty Tiger Warriors, but besides the ceremonial escort no figure for the size of the army survives and the total number of troops is nowhere stated. As to distance, Liang marched south from Chengdu by way of Hanzhong and the interior of Yizhou into Yuexi and Dianchi, a march measured in thousands of li. Geographically, Pei Songzhi's note quoting the Hanshu Dizhi says that the Luo River rises at Guting in Zangke commandery, and the May crossing was made on that water; Dianchi was the goal of the march. On supplies, Liang himself wrote that they 'ate for two days on one day's rations', which shows how tight the rationing became once the army went deep; after the pacification the opposite holds, for 'the army's supplies came from it and the state was enriched', and the southern resources of cinnabar, salt, copper and horses began to feed Shu Han steadily. Nothing has been recorded about the number of crossbows, only that their rate of fire exceeded that of the ordinary bow and that a single man could loose them in succession, which made them the core of Shu's firepower in a country without cavalry. Zhuge Liang's own collection, the Zhuge shi ji, runs to twenty-four chapters and one hundred and four thousand one hundred and twelve characters, and its third chapter is titled 'The Southern Campaign'.
cause: 南征的直接起因，是蜀漢主人的更替與益州南部的趁亂反亂。章武三年劉備崩於永安，後主劉禪即位，諸葛亮開府治事、領益州牧，蜀漢一時大喪。《三國志》記建興元年「南中諸郡，並皆叛亂」，然亮「以新遭大喪，故未便加兵」，先遣使聘吳、結和親，把心力放在東線，南中便擱置了兩年。到建興三年，內部叛亂未平，東面曹魏又在籌劃取蜀，亮若再放棄南中，便腹背同時受敵，於是先平南中、再圖北進，這正是他在《出師表》裡自述「今南方已定，兵甲已足，當獎率三軍，北定中原」的次序。值得注意的是，亮以丞相假節之權便宜行事，兵出而後奏聞，這場戰爭的決策權集中在一人之手，也讓他得以用最小的行政成本調動整個益州的人力與物資。蜀漢在漢中與南中之間的連絡線極長，一旦南中叛亂拖延日久，東線的屏障便會消失，故此役只能速戰速決。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the southern campaign was a change of ruler in Shu Han and a rising in the southern part of Yizhou during the confusion that followed. In the third year of Zhangwu Liu Bei died at Yong'an, the heir Liu Shan took the throne, Zhuge Liang opened his own office and took the governorship of Yizhou, and Shu Han was in a great bereavement. The Records of the Three Kingdoms states that in Jianxing 1 'all the southern commanderies rebelled', yet Liang, 'having newly suffered a great bereavement, did not find it convenient to send troops'; he sent envoys to Wu to make peace, turned his attention to the eastern front and left the south alone for two years. By Jianxing 3 the revolt was still unquelled and Cao Wei on the east was already planning to take Shu; if Liang abandoned the south again, Shu would face enemies on two fronts at once. He therefore decided to settle the south first and march north afterwards, which is exactly the order he sets out himself in the Memorial on Dispatching the Army: 'Now the south is settled and arms and armour are sufficient; I shall lead the three armies to bring order to the Central Plain.' It should be noted that Liang acted on the authority of his chancellorship and the imperial tally, dispatching the army first and reporting it afterwards, so the decision lay in one man's hands, and that allowed him to mobilise the manpower and materials of the whole province of Yizhou at the least administrative cost. The line of communication between Hanzhong and the south was enormously long, and once the revolt dragged on the eastern front lost its screen, so the campaign had to be finished quickly.
impact: 南平之後，蜀漢第一次真正解除了腹背之患。政治上，南中被分為益州郡、牂柯郡、越嶂郡三個行政單位，配以蜀漢官吏與當地首領共同治理，張嶷以中都護統南中軍務，標誌著雲南高原正式納入中原王朝的郡縣體系，也開啟了此後千餘年雲南與內地持續互動的格局。經濟與軍事上，軍資所出、國以富饒，蜀漢的銅、丹砂、鹽、馬來源打通，兵甲充足，才具備建興五年北伐的底氣。文化上，七擒孟獲與「攻心為上」的處置方式被後世反覆引述，成為中華兵學中最著名的安邊範例之一；諸葛亮文集自編「南征」一篇，也說明他本人把此役視為獨立可述的武功。隱憂同樣存在：南中徵發與連年北伐相疊，蜀漢末期南中人心不附，蜀亡之後滇地亦隨之生亂，說明速勝之後仍留下長遠的治理難題。就兵器而言，弩這一類不依賴戰馬、能由步兵持續施放的機射武器，也在這場戰事之後成為蜀漢軍隊的標準配備，與長槍、大盾配合，成為南方山林與北方秦雍戰場上同樣倚重的火力骨幹。
impactEn: Once the south was pacified, Shu Han was rid of its most dangerous internal enemy for the first time. Politically, the south was divided into the three administrative units of Yizhou, Zangke and Yuexi, governed jointly by Shu's officials and the local chiefs, with Zhang Yi as Protectant General of the Centre commanding the southern forces. This marked the formal incorporation of the Yunnan plateau into the commandery and county system of the Central Plains, and opened the long interaction between Yunnan and the interior that continued for more than a thousand years. Economically and militarily, 'the army's supplies came from it and the state was enriched': the sources of copper, cinnabar, salt and horses were opened, and with arms and provisions sufficient the northern expedition of Jianxing 5 became possible at last. In cultural memory, the seven captures of Meng Huo and the way the campaign was settled by attacking the heart above all have been cited again and again, and have become one of the best-known models of pacifying a frontier in the military art of China; the fact that Zhuge Liang's own collected writings include a chapter titled 'The Southern Campaign' shows that he himself regarded this campaign as a separate achievement worth recording. The risk was equally real: the levies taken from the south overlapped with years of northern campaigning, the south grew restive in Shu's last years, and when Shu fell the Dian region broke out in disorder as well, which shows that even after a quick victory a long task of government remained. As for weapons, the crossbow, a machine missile that did not depend on the warhorse and could be loosed continuously by the foot soldier, became a standard part of the Shu Han order of battle after this campaign, working together with the long spear and the great shield as the backbone of the missile fire on the southern wooded slopes and later on the northern battlefields of Qin and Yong.
result: 結局是全勝，但取勝靠的是策略而非兵力。孟獲七縱七禽之後不再反，說出「公，天威也，南人不復反矣」，亮遂率軍至滇池，宣告南中平定；同年秋，戰事全部結束。亮拒絕留兵常駐、拒絕長期運糧，用「即其渠率而用之」的方式把治理成本降到最低，只留中都護統軍、各郡守令守土，蜀漢因此得以把有限的兵力和糧食轉用於北面。他回師之後「乃治戎講武，以俟大舉」，兩年後上《出師表》，以「五月渡瀘，深入不毛」自陳艱苦，又以「今南方已定，兵甲已足」宣告可以出手。對蜀漢而言，這場戰爭最大的成果不是土地，而是一個可以放手北伐的後方；對南中而言，則是地方勢力被拆解、首領被收編，從此長期捲入蜀漢與中原的戰爭與交流。孟獲部眾遣返原地，據說其後曾隨亮至成都；此類細節史無明文，可確定的是南中自此由割據轉為郡縣化的羈縻治理。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete victory, but it was won by strategy rather than by numbers. After being released and captured seven times, Meng Huo would not rebel again and declared: 'My lord, this is Heaven's might; the people of the south will not rebel again'. Liang then marched to Dianchi and proclaimed the south pacified, and by the autumn of that year all the fighting was over. Liang refused to station a permanent garrison and refused to keep transporting grain, using the plan of 'taking their own chiefs and using them' to bring the cost of government down to the lowest level, leaving only a Protectant General in command and the commandery officials in their districts, so that Shu Han could turn its limited soldiers and grain towards the north. After returning he 'trained the troops and reviewed the military in preparation for a great undertaking', and two years later he presented the Memorial on Dispatching the Army, describing his hardship in the words 'in the fifth month we crossed the Luo, penetrating deep into the uncultivated land', and declaring, with the south settled and arms sufficient, that the northern campaign might begin. For Shu Han the chief gain of this war was not land but a rear from which it could strike the north with a free hand; for the south it meant the breaking up of the local powers, the incorporation of their chiefs, and a long-drawn involvement in the wars and exchanges of Shu Han and the Central Plains. Meng Huo's people were sent back to their own country, and it is said that some of them afterwards followed Liang to Chengdu; such details are not clearly attested, and what is certain is that the south passed from separatism to a system of commandery administration under the loose control of the centre.
